scientific_boundary: Perfused mouse BBB shows blood-facing, EPCR-dependent APC entry. Does not establish native human stroke luminal protein.
EPCR/FVIIa internalization, caveolar sensitivity and Rab11 recycling in cultured peripheral EC or CHO-EPCR.
Receptor-dependent native APC tracer blood-to-brain uptake in healthy mice; no synthetic peptide and intact capillary-depleted APC not independently quantified.
No direct intact engineered short-peptide or peptide-cargo basolateral recovery in reviewed studies.
Ligand-site blocking alters EPCR-dependent PAR1/Ca²⁺ signaling; nonblocking epitopes may differ. Not evidence peptide is harmful.
Effect of proposed synthetic binder on human stroke BBB integrity untested.
Protein C/APC competition at natural ligand site is demonstrated; choose/test a noncompetitive accessible epitope.
Human peripheral/tumor endothelium displays surface-accessible 8G4 epitope; no native human stroke BBB proof.
8G4-bound TM4SF1 internalizes in cultured endothelium, with intracellular/nuclear association; not abluminal BBB transport.
No polarized brainward peptide or antibody cargo transcytosis shown in reviewed studies.
No intact engineered peptide or cargo isolated from brainward basolateral receiver in reviewed studies.
TM4SF1 suppression affects endothelial repair; antibody/ADC vascular toxicity is construct- and payload-dependent, not proof of passive peptide toxicity.
Brain BBB integrity effects of a nonperturbing peptide binder unmeasured; peripheral ADC vessel damage is not BBB transport or safety test.
8G4 recognition depends on EL2 epitope and species-specific glycosylation; human-mouse binder transfer cannot be assumed.
Tumor-associated brain vascular SELP, including human medulloblastoma vasculature, studied; no native human stroke luminal proof.

Fucoidan multivalent nanoparticle uptake/caveolin-1-dependent traffic in activated tumor-brain endothelial models. Independent cell systems show P-selectin endosomal/lysosomal sorting, not peptide BBB transit.
Brainward nanoparticle transport in tumor-model BBB; not general ischemic-stroke free-peptide transport.
No receptor-specific intact short-peptide BBB cargo recovery; tumor nanoparticle integrity not equivalent.
Platelet/leukocyte adhesion and inflammatory activation are biologically documented; risk depends on binder, dose and stroke model.
SELP-linked stroke vascular inflammation associates with BBB permeability; leakage is not transcytosis or proof proposed peptide disrupts BBB.
BBB delivery precedent involves multivalent fucoidan nanocarriers; free peptide avidity and mechanism remain untested.
ECSCR membrane localization observed in cultured human peripheral EC; brain luminal epitope not demonstrated.
KDR-associated endosomal redistribution observed; NOT selective uptake of ECSCR-binding cargo.
No ECSCR-dependent brainward transport experiment in reviewed studies.
No intact ECSCR-binding short-peptide BBB receiver assay in reviewed studies.
ECSCR gain/loss affects VEGFR2 signaling, endothelial migration and metabolism; not ligand-specific peptide toxicity.
Direct BBB integrity response to an ECSCR-targeting peptide not studied.
Cross-species extracellular identity is ~46%; no validated human luminal docking epitope or corresponding glycan-aware binder.
ACKR1 reported on inflamed brain microvessels (EAE/MS context), not validated ischemic human stroke luminal target.
ACKR1-associated chemokine uptake and trafficking in BBB/venular models; evidence is for chemokines, not peptides.
Direct BBB observation is tissue/abluminal-to-blood/luminal chemokine transport, not brainward. This is construct-/ligand-specific.
No intact engineered blood-to-brain short-peptide delivery shown.
ACKR1 chemokine presentation/recruitment and inflammatory-cell trafficking documented; proposed peptide consequences untested.
Direct peptide-binder effect on tight-junction integrity not measured; EAE leukocyte recruitment is a distinct endpoint.
Extracellular chemokine-binding N terminus provides structural context but does not establish safe noncompeting peptide access.
Human brain capillary LRP1 protein and uptake studies support target context; native human stroke luminal polarity unquantified.
Angiopep-2/L57 brain EC-associated fluorescence/transport precedents; receptor dependency and routing are incompletely resolved.
Apical-to-basolateral Angiopep-2 signal in BBB model and mouse parenchymal tracer; in-vivo LRP1 exclusivity and cargo integrity not demonstrated.
In-vitro intact Angiopep-2 receiver signal reported with underlying chromatograms not shown; chemically verified intact brain parenchymal peptide/cargo absent.
LRP1 has broad endogenous clearance functions; test competition of specific peptide, not automatically inferred toxicity.
Proposed comparator peptide effects on BBB junctions and barrier integrity not established in selected evidence.
LRP1 extracellular cluster-IV and broad ligands require peptide-level epitope, polarity and endogenous ligand competition tests.
